title: Higher coefficient sum and tail identity
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\mathrm{law}$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, let $r,j$ be natural numbers, and let $t\in\mathbb R$. The sum of the even-moment coefficient gaps times $t^{2l}$ over integers $l$ with $j<l\le r$ equals $-t^{2j}$ times the higher even-moment coefficient tail at $t$.
hypotheses_covered: $\mathrm{law}$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
